op.text:
TASK: annotate ONE English sentence in UMR (PropBank-style numbered roles) in EXACTLY the conventions below. Reuse variables of the 5 previous sentences for coref and temporal links. For every event verb/adjective call roleset_lookup(lemma) to pick the sense and check which roles are core (-01 if no roleset fits).

1. EVENTS
Events: predicated verbs, states, non-verbal clauses; event nominals (storm, meeting); participles; gerunds; infinitives; relative-clause verbs.
NOT events: modal/tense auxiliaries (will, would, can, may, must, should, have, be, do); phasal verbs (start, keep, stop, finish: only aspect); the light verb of light verb + eventive noun (use the noun, interview-01); adjectives/state nouns used as modifiers; entity nouns.
- Predicate adjectives/nouns that have a PropBank roleset ARE events: "X is important" -> (i/ important-01 :ARG1 X :aspect state); "the basket is full" -> (f/ full-09 :ARG1 basket :ARG2 (t/ thing)) (an unexpressed ARG2 = implicit thing, aligned 0-0, coref to the earlier noun it stands for). Use have-mod-91 etc. only if roleset_lookup finds nothing.
- A particle after get/go/come (down, up, out, away) is its own concept: "gets down out of the tree" -> (g/ get-05 :ARG1 mover :ARG2 (d/ down-03) :source tree). Do not fuse into get-down-01. Directional/locative PPs that are not core roles: :goal (into, to), :source (out of, from), :place, :path.
- Sentence-initial But/However (contrast with the previous sentence): root (h/ have-concession-91 :ARG1 (e/ event) :ARG2 <main clause>); h aligned to the connective, e aligned 0-0, coref (earlier-event :same-event e). h has no aspect.
- "know/ask/wonder if/whether X (or not)": (k/ know-01 :ARG1 (t/ truth-value :polarity-of (x/ X-event ...))); t aligned to "if"; do not build or/have-mod pairs for "or not".
- "I don't think/believe/expect X": the negation goes on X (:polarity - on X's event), not on think.
- "make/let X do" = two events. Add implicit events only when sure.

2. ROOT
One main event is root; complement, adverbial, relative events hang under it. Clear relation (:purpose :cause :condition :concession :manner :temporal before/after/while) -> role under the main event. No clear relation: root = and / or (:op1 :op2) or contrast-91 / but-91 / unexpected-co-occurrence-91 (:ARG1 :ARG2). A clause that starts with and/and then just continues the narrative: annotate the clause itself as root (no and node); the link is in the document-level temporal group. Non-verbal clauses: abstract predicate is root: have-91 (ARG1 possessor, ARG2 possessum), belong-91 (possessum, possessor), exist-91 (location, theme), have-place-91 (theme, location), have-mod-91 (theme, property), have-role-91 (theme, reference, category), have-org-role-92 (theme, org, title), have-rel-role-92 (theme, relative, role), identity-91 (theme, equated).

3. CONCEPTS AND ROLES
- Events: PropBank lemma-sense. Nouns: plain lemma. Time words are concepts under :temporal: (t/ then), (a/ at-first), (t/ today), (n/ now).
- Pronouns/implicit people: (p/ person :refer-person 1st|2nd|3rd :refer-number singular|plural). Generic "you" adds :refer-definiteness class. Common nouns: :refer-number singular|plural. Named entities: type + (n/ name :op1 ..) + :wiki, no refer-person. Pronoun "that/this" = (t/ thing :mod (d/ that)) with t aligned to the word and d 0-0.
- Core roles per roleset; reentrancy by shared variable (control: wants to go -> go :ARG0 same person). Passive: same roles as active. Inverse roles for modifying events: (p/ person :ARG0-of (r/ run-02)).
- Kinship/titles: (p/ person :ARG1-of (h/ have-rel-role-92 :ARG2 rel :ARG3 (f/ father))) and have-org-role-92.
- Non-core: :temporal :place :manner :purpose :cause :condition :concession :duration :frequency :direction :path :extent :goal :source; noun relations :mod :poss (owner; possessum is parent) :part :topic :medium :age :group :example :quant (all, numbers) :unit :ord :li :polite :degree. Measures: substance is the head (three cups of milk -> milk :quant 3 :unit cup).
- Dates: date-entity (:year :month :day :weekday :time). Durations: temporal-quantity :quant :unit. Negation: :polarity - on the negated concept.

4. ATTRIBUTES in the graph (all lowercase values, written after roles)
- :aspect on each event except abstract have-concession-91: process (event nominal) > habitual (generic/usual, used to) > state (be/have/love/know/want/think/see, perception, mental, ability, non-verbal, adjective events) > activity (progressive/present, no end, start/keep) > endeavor (stopped, for-duration) > performance (completed or future; default; telic motion or transfer like dump, get down). imperfective / perfective only if unsure.
- :mode imperative | interrogative | expressive on the main verb; imperatives get a 2nd-person ARG0.
- DO NOT write :modstr or :modpred in the graph. The complement of a modal-type predicate (want, need, think, believe, expect, hope, try, plan, decide, know-if, allow, forbid) stays its ARG1 and ALSO gets :modal-predicate <predicate variable> (bare variable). :temporal (parent :rel child): rel describes the CHILD relative to the PARENT, so (A :after B) means B happens after A; (A :before B) means B is before A; (A :overlap B); (A :contained B) means B is inside A. Entries: (time-expression-node :contained event) for an overt time expression (at first, then); otherwise link the event to the nearest relevant earlier event: narrative sequence (and then, next action) -> (earlier :after current); same time (state, comment) -> (earlier :overlap current); complement of think/know -> (earlier-context-event :overlap complement). If nothing clear, give no temporal tuple.
:modal starts with (root :modal author); then (author :label event). Labels: full-affirmative, partial-affirmative, neutral-affirmative, full-negative, partial-negative, neutral-negative, unspecified. Plain asserted event: (author :full-affirmative e). Gold: researchers -> person :ARG0-of research-01; workers -> work-01; spokeswoman -> have-org-role-92; findings/results/filters/symptoms -> thing :ARG1-of find-01 and similar; high-02, old-01, new-02, filter-02, result-01. problems.pattern: Temporal expressions have the wrong structure. 'N years ago' should be before :op1 now :quant more-than/temporal-quantity. problems.pattern: Speech/report structure. The reported clause should carry :quote and be linked to the speaker. Repeated mentions (crocidolite, Lorillard, problem/story) are not linked in coref. A same-sentence pronoun (it, its) is a new thing node instead of reusing the antecedent variable.
problems.evidence: S1 g_reentrancy quote/ARG2 asbestos missing. S3 possessor/ARG0 reentrancy missing. j_coref_chain missing in S3, S4, S5.

problems.pattern: Phasal 'stop' is declared a non-event in the skill, but gold keeps stop-01 :ARG1 use-01. Concession 'Although' and appositives were handled inconsistently.

reflect.reflection: Most lost units are systematic conventions, not random errors. The critic and finalizer invent rules the gold does not use: refer-number singular everywhere, retyping to organization, wiki '-'. The generator also forbids document-creation-time, which gold uses constantly. And nobody checks the mechanical format: sN variable prefixes, 'sNs0', the (root :modal author) first tuple, alignment lines for every variable. I will do four things. (1) Fix the generate, critique and finalize skills so they agree with gold on refer-number (plural only), company/product/journal types, real wikis, document-creation-time, the speaker modal tree and :quote. (2) Add compact decomposition rules (agent nouns, deverbal entity nouns, adjective senses, 'ago/once/later', same-sentence pronoun reuse, stop-01). (3) Make the critic report omissions of these patterns instead of pushing the harmful ones. (4) Add a deterministic rule step, with tests, that repairs variable prefixes, 'sNs0', the modal root tuple, missing or stray alignment lines, and strips :refer-number singular from nodes without :refer-person. It has no model cost. I keep edits small to stay under the 10000-character limit.

The small models write surface-lemma graphs. They skip the sense lookup for modifiers and deverbal nouns, omit nested aspects, and do not build abstract structures such as have-degree-91, temporal-quantity and say-91. The critic adds noise: it flips correct :contains and modal labels and extends the modal-predicate list. The finalize step silently drops (root :modal author), and names come out unquoted. I will do five things.
- Add a deterministic rule step after finalize that quotes :opN and :wiki strings and guarantees (root :modal author) is first in the modal group. This is a pure format fix that models do badly.
- Add a compact block to generate on deverbal and adjective senses, universal aspect, comparatives, quantities, 'according to' and agent compounds. I pay for it by trimming two low-value sentences, so the skill stays under 10000 characters.
- Make 'continue' an event, and drop think/believe/expect/assume from the modal-predicate list, in all three skills, because gold has no such reentrancy.
- Stop the critic from over-correcting: :contains for present states and the modal cue list are correct as written.
- Remind finalize to keep root modal, aspect and sense ids.

import re


def fix_graph(g: str) -> str:
    """Quote bare :opN and :wiki values in the sentence-level graph text."""
    def q(m):
        v = m.group(2)
        if re.fullmatch(r'-?\d+(\.\d+)?', v) or re.fullmatch(r's\d+[a-z]\d*', v):
            return m.group(0)
        return m.group(1) + '"' + v + '"'
    g = re.sub(r'(:op\d+\s+)([^\s()"]+)', q, g)
    g = re.sub(r'(:wiki\s+)([^\s()"-][^\s()"]*)', lambda m: m.group(1) + '"' + m.group(2) + '"', g)

def run(annotation: str, sentence: dict) -> str:
    """Repair a UMR annotation string.

    Quotes unquoted :opN / :wiki string values in the sentence-level graph
    (leaving numbers, variable references and '-' alone), and ensures the
    document-level modal structure has a '(root :modal author)' entry, replacing
    a bogus '(sNs0 :modal author)' root if present. Returns the annotation
    unchanged if it has no '# alignment:' section.
    """
    i = annotation.find('# alignment:')
    if i < 0:
        return annotation
    j = annotation.find('# document level annotation:')
    graph = fix_graph(annotation[:i])
    if j < 0:
        return graph + annotation[i:]
    mid = annotation[i:j]
    doc = annotation[j:]
    doc = re.sub(r'\(\s*s\d+s0\s+:modal\s+author\s*\)', '(root :modal author)', doc)
    if re.search(r':modal\s*\(', doc) and 'root :modal author' not in doc:
        doc = re.sub(r'(:modal\s*\()\s*\(', lambda m: m.group(1) + '(root :modal author)\n            (', doc, count=1)
    return graph + mid + doc

reflect.reflection: The small models drift from the output conventions in three ways: variable naming, the alignment unit, and which events carry aspect and modality. These are mostly mechanical, so I add a final rule step, `clean_doc`, that fixes what code can fix. It renames bare variables to the sN prefix everywhere. It drops tuples that use undefined or bare variables. It removes modal tuples for modifier-adjective events that have no aspect. It forces `(root :modal author)` first, since that is missing in the final output of all five sentences. I infer N from the `(sNs0 / sentence` header, not from the sentence index. The skill edits are small. I fix the contradictory 'EVERY event has :aspect' rule in all three skills. generate is near its character budget, so I trim it first. I put the new lexical and structural patterns mainly in finalize, which has room. These cover yield-03 as root for 'had a yield of X%', down-03 for 'down from', over-05 with a degree attribute, current/depends-on for 'currently', one head word per alignment, ARG0 for the owner of a deverbal noun, one temporal parent per event, and the coref subset direction. I also add guards to critique so it stops demanding :poss, product retyping, or aspect on modifiers. The gold is inconsistent about :refer-number on plural nouns. S12, S13 and S15 have it, while S14, S16 and earlier groups do not. I leave that rule unchanged.

operations.text:
- Variables: all s<N><letter><digits> of THIS sentence, never bare (b, y2); alignment lines and doc tuples use the same names; no tuple with an undefined variable.
- Alignment: ONE head word per node; no spans over compounds/hyphenated words (money-fund: money 3-3, fund 5-5; 'seven-day': quant node on 'seven', unit day on 'day').
- 'had/has a (N-day) yield of X%' and 'The yield was X%': the event noun is the root (y/ yield-03 :ARG0 owner :ARG1 (percentage-entity :value X) :duration (temporal-quantity :quant N :unit day) :ARG1-of compound-01 / simple-02); no have-91, no thing wrapper; 'average' -> value :ARG2-of average-01.
- 'down/up from M%': the current value gets :ARG1-of (d/ down-03 :ARG2 (percentage-entity :value M)); never decline-01 with ARG3/ARG4.
- 'over/above N' (also 'well over'): (o/ over-05 :ARG2 N-node :degree intensifier), not more-than; heavily/well/very = :degree intensifier, no node. 'currently' -> (c/ current) :temporal; doc: (document-creation-time :depends-on c), NOT (c :contained e).
- Adjective modifiers take roleset senses via roleset_lookup (top -> top-06, 'Typically' -> :ARG1-of (typical-02) on the main event, short-07, comparable-03 :ARG1 compared node). 'management fees' = fee :purpose (manage-01); 'dollar-denominated' = denominate-01 :ARG2 dollar; 'overseas' = :place.
- 'its yield': possessor of a deverbal noun is ARG0 of the event ((t/ thing :ARG1-of (y/ yield-03 :ARG0 owner))), not :poss. 'which V...' about a whole clause: (clause-event :ARG0-of (v/ V-01 ...)), not :mod.
- Temporal: each event has ONE temporal parent. Present/habitual main event: (document-creation-time :contains main); past: (document-creation-time :before main); nested event nominals/modifier clauses: (main :overlap nested); inside a state/activity: (outer :contains inner).
- Coref subset: (whole :subset-of part), the later part/member is second: earlier 'funds', later 'the top funds' -> (earlier :subset-of later). Same reference repeated -> :same-entity to the earliest mention.
operations.reason: Constructions and conventions that cost the most units in this group.

reflect.reflection: The small models follow the written conventions literally. Several of those conflict with this gold: the critique and finalize say particle -> :path, the critique says and-roots only for unrelated clauses, and the critique prefers include-91 for part nouns. The critique also issues confident but wrong rewrites that finalize applies. The roleset_lookup tool shows only the first 14 senses and never lists phrasal rolesets, so get-up-26 is invisible when the model looks up 'get'. I make four kinds of change. (1) Extend roleset_lookup to append phrasal rolesets, and tell generate and finalize to look up 'verb particle' and use one fused concept. (2) Fix the contradictory critique and finalize rules: particles take :direction with a sense id; clause-joining and/consecutive roots are not demoted; no verb swapping; part nouns use :part-of. (3) Add a final rule that drops modal tuples for sense-id nodes with no own :aspect. (4) Add a short coref reminder. I freed space in generate by removing duplicated text. I left imperative handling unchanged because the guideline asks for a 2nd-person ARG0 and this gold looks inconsistent with it.

reflect.reflection:
Most of the cost is over-tagging in financial reports, extra or misplaced TLINKs, and a few value/class details. I first free space in generate, which is near its budget, with small deletions of duplicated text. Then I add compact rules:
- Comparison and explanation participles ('compared with', 'reflecting') and measure subjects of rise/fall ('profit', 'net') are not tagged.
- post/report(ed) + profit/earnings/loss is REPORTING.
- A timex from the previous sentence that frames the current one is linked to the main event, with no t0 link.
- 'nearly' maps to LESS_THAN.
- 'last year' beside a quarter or month period means the same period a year earlier.
Finalize and critique get matching rules. They cover applying the untag finding, limiting IDENTITY to true light verbs, and keeping a 'nine months' period as DURATION. I do not try to learn the inconsistent gold choices on financial-noun classes, such as loss OCCURRENCE vs gains STATE, or the odd missing first 'included'.

reflect.reflection: Small models follow the written rules literally, and several rules disagree with the gold. The skills tag light-verb nominals and link them IDENTITY, give nouns tense NONE, and treat cross-sentence links as optional. The gold chains each sentence's main event to the previous one and puts reported events BEFORE the saying verb. It uses SIMULTANEOUS for light verb + noun, tags idioms such as take part and pay tribute as the verb only, and splits year ranges into two DATE tags. I edit generate, finalize and critique to say the same thing. I also add a rule step after finalize that rebuilds the sentence from the original text when the model output has preamble text, added quotes or altered text. It re-inserts the tags by sequential search and removes duplicate TLINKs. Some gold labels look idiosyncratic (helped=I_STATE, do tense PRESENT with no modality, no time link for expedition), so I did not teach those.

reflect.reflection: The small models over-annotate generic commentary sentences and force cross-sentence links, while missing the within-sentence structure the gold actually has: attitude adjective plus its infinitive and participle complements, and an infinitive complement linked SIMULTANEOUS to its governing verb. reflect.reflection: The weak TLINK scores come from linking style. The generator chains adjunct and complement events to each other and adds extra pairwise or t0 links, while the gold links each such event to the governing verb only. The critique also overrode a correct class ('keep' ASPECTUAL) and called valid tense values invalid. Class vocabulary was incomplete: allow/permit/let/help should be I_ACTION, and ordinary non-copular verbs like 'benefit' should not be STATE. The generator also tags causative 'have' and misses coordinated nouns. Several gold choices are inconsistent with earlier groups: INFINITIVE vs PRESENT for infinitives, noun tense, DURATION for '2008'. I do not learn those. The generate skill is near its budget, so I first delete low-value or duplicated text (the 'at the same time' and 'now' sentences, the light-verb duplicate, the 'between X and Y' clause, the 'two years ago' example, the redundant-nominal rule) and then add compact rules. The same class fixes go into critique and finalize so they are not reverted.

reflect.reflection: The small models over-annotate opinion-column prose. They treat every verb as an event and chain links between them, but the gold keeps only the verbs that govern an intention or a speech act, plus their direct complement. The generate skill is near the budget, so I first free about 270 characters by deleting rules that finalize and critique already repeat. Then I add short rules to generate: no events in generic, evaluative, comparative or 'the way' clauses; no possessive 'have'; no t0 link for habitual or opinion statements; intend and assure are I_ACTION. Finalize and critique have room, so they get the fuller pruning rules, including the performative 'can assure' as PRESENT with no modality and IS_INCLUDED in t0. The gold is inconsistent on infinitive tense, so I leave that alone.

reflect.reflection: The costliest errors were the critique and finalize steps undoing correct output. They deleted the event on 'led', deleted 'upset' while trying to narrow its extent, and replaced SIMULTANEOUS with IS_INCLUDED for -ing adjuncts. Several overgeneral rules were behind this. 'Participles modifying a noun are not events' is too broad, and so are 'keep is always ASPECTUAL' and 'adjunct events are IS_INCLUDED'. I narrow each of these rules and add a few lexical and value facts: a SET value for 'every morning', REPORTING for acknowledge, and OCCURRENCE for 'forced'. Generate is near the size budget, so I first cut low-value text (possessive 'have', the yesterday/today/tomorrow line and a parenthetical) to make room. I do not chase the gold's internal inconsistencies, such as INFINITIVE versus PRESENT, which links hang off 'said' versus 'vowed', and whether to tag light-verb 'make'.

reflect.reflection: Most losses are in TLINKs, where gold is inconsistent and I do not chase it. Clear, general errors are: event nouns missed, modals dropped from the copied text, classes of mean/indicate, and the critique pushing event nouns to I_ACTION. I free space in generate by deleting obvious text, then add short rules to generate, critique and finalize. I leave out the infinitive tense, the 'denied' class and the noun-tense items because the gold is inconsistent across rounds.
